reason: The PROBLEM is real and reproduces; the PROPOSED FIX is wrong, so the finding is refuted with the fix corrected below. Confirmed against source and frames: lately.html:277 is `.kpi.lead { background: var(--ink); border-color: var(--ink); color: var(--paper); }` with no dark override anywhere (the only `[data-v="dark"]` rules are lines 92, 245, 317), and dark `--ink` is `#ffffff` (line 96) over a `--paper-2` ground of `#0f0f10`. In shots/dark-full--1440x960.png the denominator card is exactly what the seat describes: a ~285x230 pure-white slab, the largest bright region on the page by an order of magnitude, sitting in a row whose actual status marks are 3px indigo meters that read as nothing beside it. It is worse than the seat claims: at max-width 900px (line 438) `.kpi.lead` takes `grid-column: 1 / -1`, so at 390 and 768 the white plate is a full-width band across a near-black page, on the device most likely to be read at night. Class `defect` is correct and not overstated: nothing untrue is asserted and the product still does its job, but the row's emphasis visibly inverts after dark. Two corrections to the seat's framing: the light plate is not the 'quiet' object either -- pure black on #fafafa is also the highest-contrast object in that row, so this is not a contrast asymmetry but a luminance/halation one, which is why no gate catches it. Now the fix, which fails on two counts. (1) It breaks WCAG AA outright. `background: var(--paper-3)` gives a #27272a plate, but the fix never names the two rules that would survive it: `.kpi.lead` still carries `color: var(--paper)`, which in dark is #18181b, putting the OPEN NOW label and the 9 at 1.19:1 on that plate; and `.kpi.lead .t-small` (line 278) still pins 'jobs not finished' to `--mark-ctx` #3f3f46, which is 1.43:1. Both are hard failures the audit gate would reject on the next run. The fix gestures at 'numeral and label at var(--ink) and var(--ink-3)' but never says to unset the inherited `color`, and never mentions `.t-small` at all. (2) Its numbers, though correctly read off the source, are the wrong ones. #27272a against sibling cards at `--paper` #18181b is a 1.19:1 luminance step -- all but invisible -- so the denominator would stop reading as a categorically different object and become a marginally lighter sixth card, resting its whole identity on a #71717a hairline. The shared denominator is a protected object; the plate being a different KIND of surface is how a reader knows the 9 is the thing the other four are counted out of, not another status. Trading a glare problem for a weakened protected object is not an improvement at this bar.
sharpenedFix: Keep the inverted plate, take it off pure white. One rule, nothing else touched: `[data-v="dark"] .kpi.lead { background: var(--ink-2); border-color: var(--ink-2); }` -- #d4d4d8, Ink 5 in the eighteen. That cuts emitted luminance 34% (relative luminance 1.000 to 0.661) and removes the pure-white extreme, while the card stays unmistakably an inverted plate, so the protected shared-denominator reading survives intact. Crucially it needs no text changes and no new rules: the inherited `color: var(--paper)` #18181b lands at 11.98:1 on #d4d4d8, and the existing `.kpi.lead .t-small` at `--mark-ctx` #3f3f46 lands at 7.07:1 -- both comfortably AA, both already written. The light rule at line 277 is untouched, exactly as the seat asked. If the founder wants a deeper cut, `--ink-3` #a1a1aa is the next step down (64% luminance cut, label and numeral still 6.91:1) but it costs a second rule, because `.t-small` at #3f3f46 falls to 4.08:1 there and would have to move to `var(--paper-2)` #0f0f10 at 7.48:1 -- and a mid-grey plate starts to lose the authority the anchor card needs. Prefer `--ink-2`.
breaks: Low blast radius, but three things to re-check. (1) Re-run audit.mjs: the WCAG check composites against the real backdrop, and all three type roles on this card (t-label, t-num, t-small) change backdrop, so all three must be re-read even though the computed ratios above say they pass. (2) The card carries `box-shadow: 0 1px 2px var(--shadow)` where dark `--shadow` is rgba(15,15,16,0.6) -- a dark shadow under a light plate on a dark ground is invisible-to-muddy; check it does not read as a smear at the plate's lower edge, and drop it for this card in dark if it does. (3) Re-shoot all four dark widths, not just 1440: at 390 and 768 the plate is full-width (line 438), which is where the original glare is worst and where the new value has to be judged. `.sk-wrap .kpi.lead` (line 380) already overrides background to `--paper` for the skeleton, so dark-loading is unaffected -- confirm that override still wins after the new rule is added, since a `[data-v="dark"]` selector outranks it on specificity; if it does, scope the new rule as `[data-v="dark"] .kpi.lead:not(.sk-wrap *)` or place the skeleton override after it. That specificity collision is the one real regression risk here and it applies equally to the seat's version of the fix.
